humanities_role_explanation: Comics (AI-generated pages and Manga109 pages) and culture labels supply the stimuli, but the competence tested is general MLLM cultural awareness (object/culture recognition, conflict detection, Japanese-to-X machine translation). No disciplinary humanities competence (comics studies, cultural history) is targeted; cultural conflict is defined as co-occurrence of cultures in one image.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Comic page images (generated by Doubao, or from Manga109) paired with text questions; the translation task gives a Japanese source sentence plus the comic page and requires text output.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Q1 is multi-answer multiple-choice background culture identification; Q2 is multiple-choice selection of culturally representative objects (culture-aware object extraction); Q3 is yes/no identification of cultural conflict; Q4 is free-text description of conflicts in the format 'Something should not be in Some Culture'; Q5 is Japanese-to-EN/DE/RU/ES/TH manga dialog machine translation labelled 'cultural content generation'.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to cultural awareness of MLLMs using comics; three tasks within one domain rather than a broad multi-task general benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 11 open-source MLLMs: SPHINX, Monkey, MiniGPT-v2, mPLUG-Owl3, LLaVA-1.5-7B, LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OV, InternLM-XC2.5, Llama3.2, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy, composite CACC, BLEU, COMET, BLEURT.

summary: C3B is a comic-based benchmark of 2,220 images and 18,789 QA pairs for assessing the cultural awareness of MLLMs through culture recognition, cultural conflict detection and multilingual translation. Evaluation of 11 open-source MLLMs shows low scores and a large gap to human performance, with weaker recognition of lesser-known cultures.
key_findings: Qwen2.5-VL is best overall (Q1 53.7 ACC, Q4 CACC 34.2; JA-EN BLEU 13.2). Q4 ACC is near zero for all models (max 3.87). Humans beat models in all tiers (e.g. easy Q1 92.0 vs 48.0). JA-TH is the weakest pair and JA-EN the strongest. Models recognize well-known cultures (Cambodia, Japan) better than lesser-known ones (Finnish, Somalia).
facets_explanation: Cultures and objects lists were annotated manually by students (undergrad annotation, graduate review) using Wikipedia; Q4 conflict answers were generated by DeepSeek-V3 then manually verified; and the 16,743 translation references were generated by a DeepSeek Translator/Reviewer agent loop with manual verification, so most items are model-generated. Annotators were mostly students, three graduates doing culture-related research, with inter-annotator agreement of 76.8% reported as quality control. Q1 admits 1 to 5 correct options.
results_explanation: Best Q1 result is 'Qwen2.5-VL 53.7' (accuracy, Table 3). Largest format/scoring gap, derived from Table 3: Qwen2.5-VL Q4 ACC 3.20 vs CACC 34.2 gives 31.0, rounded to 31 points (Llama3.2 2.76 vs 32.6 gives 29.8; InternLM-XC2.5 1.94 vs 29.8 gives 27.9). Other comparisons are smaller: Table 7 model Q1 by tier 48.0 (easy) vs 25.7 (hard) is 22.3 points (difficulty); Table 8 Qwen2.5-VL JA-ES BLEU 1.32 with OCR vs 14.5 without is 13.2 BLEU points (input). Human gap derived from Table 7 easy tier, same 100 sampled questions: human Q1 92.0 minus 'Model Performance' 48.0 is 44 points. The 53.7 in Table 3 is on the full set, not the sampled tier, so it is not the comparator; Table 7's model figure may be an average across models, since the paper does not say it is the best model. Fig. 5 shows higher error on lesser-known cultures.

humanities_role.quote: C3B is a novel comic-centric benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate MLLMs’ cultural awareness capabilities.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We adhered strictly to the official inference example codes provided by the respective model developers.

gold_source.quote: For the task Generation@Culture, annotation refers to the process of creating ground-truth translations.
we implemented an annotation pipeline consisting of two stages with the help of Deepseek-V3

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: The quality of annotation is ensured by credible online resources (e.g. Wikipedia).

answer_multiplicity.quote: Multiple valid answers may exist for a single question.

plurality_treatment.quote: The inter-annotator agreement score was determined to be 76.8%.

reported_format_gap.quote: From the results, it is evident that OCR significantly degrades model performance.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: ACC refers to the accuracy of Q4 calculated without referencing answers to Q1 and Q2.

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: representative cultures (e.g., Cambodia and Japan) are reliably identified, while lesser-known cultures (e.g., Finnish and Somalia) exhibit notably higher error rates.
